messages.content: Okay, I am ready to lock Sacramento. Sofia's Saturday release is set, so no Friday flight. Can you sanity-check the flights, hotel, and car before I hit pay?

Yes. Use the Saturday morning Delta nonstop from SLC to Sacramento and the Monday early-afternoon return. That keeps Sunday unrushed and avoids the holiday-weekend drive. Before you pay, one seat question: for the four of you, is the priority all sitting together, or would you split into window pairs if that is the only way?
Together first. If there are two window-and-middle pairs near each other, grab those. I do not want one kid stuck across the plane.

Good. Choose two pairs in adjacent rows if possible, with an adult in each pair. If the map cannot keep all four together, do not pay extra for scattered window seats; keep the group together and check again 24 hours before departure.
Hotel option is the refundable Rancho Cordova two-queen room. It includes breakfast and parking, cancellation is Thursday by 6 pm, and it is farther from the ceremony than I wanted.

I would book that one. The distance is the acceptable trade-off: you get two queen beds, breakfast, free parking, and flexibility. For dinner, plan on casual food near the hotel Saturday night rather than driving back toward the ceremony area after a travel day.
Car-wise, intermediate SUV? We will have four carry-ons, a garment bag, and probably Sofia's backpack. Also, graduation clothes in carry-ons?

Intermediate or midsize SUV is enough. Put the garment bag and one ceremony outfit per person in carry-ons; do not let those ride in checked luggage. Pick up the car right after landing, and assume 30 to 45 minutes from touchdown to leaving the rental lot.
We will miss at least the first part of my sister's Saturday lunch. Can you give me the simple timeline and receipt notes?

Timeline: Saturday land late morning, pick up the SUV, text your sister from the car, and join lunch when you can. Keep snacks handy. Saturday evening: easy dinner near the Rancho Cordova hotel. Sunday: hotel breakfast, ceremony and brunch, then family time without moving hotels. Monday: breakfast, check out, return the car with a fuel receipt, and fly home early afternoon. Save flight confirmations, hotel folio, rental agreement, gas receipt, and any cancellation emails.

messages.content: Next trip: late-June admissions institute in Kansas City. Registration opens Sunday evening 5 to 7, workshops are Monday and Tuesday, and there is an optional campus-partner breakfast Wednesday morning before flights home. I need flight and hotel options from SLC, preferably not a stressful connection.
Got it. Two quick things before I narrow it: is the hotel cap measured all-in with taxes and parking, and are you planning to rent a car or rely on walking and rideshare?

Cap is effectively all-in for reimbursement. The conference hotel looks okay at the base rate, but with taxes and parking it goes over. I do not need a car if the hotel is close enough. Included breakfast would help because the Monday and Tuesday mornings start early.

For Sunday outbound, I would compare three windows: 1) Morning departure: safest for registration, but eats most of Sunday. 2) Midday or early-afternoon with one connection: likely best balance if the layover is comfortable and arrival is around dinner time. 3) Later afternoon or evening: cheapest sometimes, but it makes 5 to 7 registration too tight or impossible.
That is exactly the worry. If I miss registration, I am not sure they will make Monday morning easy. Delta is fine if it is comparable, but I care more about not sprinting through a connection.

Then treat the later arrival as a backup only. Look for one connection with at least about an hour between flights, not a 35-minute airport dash. A Delta route through Minneapolis or another orderly hub is worth considering if the price is close; if another carrier gives a calmer connection and similar arrival, take the calmer itinerary.
What about coming home Wednesday? The breakfast is optional, but it may be useful.

Return trade-off: a late-morning or midday flight works only if you skip most of breakfast or leave immediately after it, then move fast on checkout and rideshare. A mid- or late-afternoon flight lets you attend breakfast, answer email for an hour, and get to the airport without a tight handoff. I would avoid anything before noon unless the agenda changes.
Hotel options are the bigger mess. The conference hotel is adjacent to sessions and has restaurants, but it is over cap once parking is in. What nearby options should I hold?

Shortlist: A) Conference hotel: easiest walk and on-site food, but reimbursement risk and parking pushes it over. B) Nearby business hotel within a short walk or 5-minute rideshare: best practical choice if it includes weekday breakfast and free or cheaper parking. C) Cheaper hotel farther out: may meet cap, but you will spend the savings on rideshares and lose convenience after evening events.
I am okay with a short walk in daylight, but I do not want to be hunting for dinner after sessions. It is just me, so a queen room is fine.

Then hold the nearby business hotel if it is refundable. Check three items before clicking: breakfast hours on Monday and Tuesday, whether there are casual dinner spots within a block or two, and the exact cancellation deadline in local time. A queen room is fine; do not pay extra for the conference block unless reimbursement approves the overage.
Should I hold flights now too, or wait for the agenda packet next week?

I would hold the hotel tonight because refundable rooms under cap can disappear. For flights, wait if fares are stable, but do not wait on the Sunday midday window if there is a 24-hour cancellation option and the price is reasonable. The registration timing makes schedule reliability more important than saving a small amount.
Give me the order of operations so I do not overthink it.

Do this: 1) Hold the refundable nearby business hotel under the cap, with breakfast verified. 2) Put the conference hotel on the waitlist only if it does not require a deposit or if reimbursement pre-approval is likely. 3) Watch Sunday midday or early-afternoon one-connection flights that arrive before registration closes; avoid short layovers. 4) For Wednesday, favor mid- or late-afternoon unless the partner breakfast gets canceled. 5) Keep screenshots of the hotel rate, taxes, parking, cancellation deadline, and the conference hotel over-cap comparison for reimbursement.

messages.content: Kansas City update: agenda packet landed. Wednesday breakfast is helpful but not required, Tuesday group dinner moved to a restaurant south of the meeting hotel, and the conference hotel is waitlist only. The nearby business hotel still has a refundable queen room under cap with weekday breakfast. I think this is the day to book.

Yes, book the nearby business hotel. The conference hotel being waitlist-only plus the Tuesday dinner moving off-site weakens the main reason to pay over cap. Before booking, capture the rate page with taxes, breakfast listed, and the cancellation deadline.
Cancellation is Sunday before arrival at 6 pm hotel local time. Breakfast is listed 6:30 to 9 weekdays. Sessions start at 8:30.
That works. Breakfast at 6:30 gives you enough margin to eat, return to the room, and leave around 8:05 or 8:10. If there is a first-day check-in line, leave a few minutes earlier Monday.

Flights: Sunday early-afternoon Delta with one connection gets me into Kansas City around 6:20. Connection is 78 minutes. Return choices are 12:10 Wednesday or 4:45 Wednesday. The 12:10 is cheaper by about $60.

Take the 4:45 return unless you need to be home earlier. The 12:10 makes the optional breakfast, checkout, and airport ride feel compressed. $60 is not enough savings to create that kind of morning squeeze.
Agreed. No one is expecting me back Wednesday afternoon. And yes, if the seat map has window seats, take those; closer to the front only if it does not mean a middle.

Flight plan: Sunday early-afternoon Delta, one connection with the 78-minute buffer; Wednesday 4:45 return. Select window seats where available, and avoid middle seats even if they are closer to the front. If a window opens later, adjust during check-in.
Do I need a rental car because of the dinner move south?

No, not for one off-site dinner. Use rideshare unless the institute offers a shuttle. A rental adds parking, reimbursement clutter, and downtown driving for very little benefit. For Monday dinner, use something walkable near the hotel or the conference area.
What should I put in the booking notes for receipts and cancellation?

Booking notes: hotel is refundable queen room under cap; cancellation deadline Sunday 6 pm local time; breakfast included 6:30 to 9 on weekdays; save folio with taxes separated. Flights: save receipt, itinerary, seat selections, and any baggage fee receipt if applicable. Ground: rideshare receipts for airport transfers and Tuesday dinner. Also keep the conference hotel waitlist and over-cap screenshot in case finance asks why you booked off-block.
Can you give me the final itinerary summary in one chunk?

Final Kansas City plan: fly from SLC Sunday early afternoon on the one-connection Delta itinerary, arriving around 6:20 pm, with window seats requested where available. Stay at the nearby refundable business hotel in a queen room under the reimbursement cap; use included weekday breakfast before Monday and Tuesday sessions. Skip the conference hotel waitlist unless a compliant room opens. Tuesday dinner: rideshare to the restaurant south of the meeting hotel. Wednesday: attend the partner breakfast if useful, check out calmly, work a bit if needed, then take the 4:45 pm return. Save hotel, flight, rideshare, and rate-comparison receipts.
